tasks.short: Prepare finance data, run statistical analyses, and interpret results.

steps.what: Agree the finance question, population, period, and intended decision.
Retrieve finance extracts and reconcile source totals.
Inspect missing values, join records, and resolve data quality exceptions.
Choose statistical methods and document assumptions.
Write and execute analysis code, then inspect numerical diagnostics.
Interpret findings and record limitations for finance users.

tasks.design: Configure approved extracts from the {ERP} into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with reconciliations and versioned transformation rules. A reusable analysis generator runs tested statistical routines and produces diagnostics; the data scientist resolves exceptions, selects methods, and records interpretation in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance definitions, source mappings, and notebook logic were scattered. Repeating an analysis often required rebuilding its preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors, statistical libraries, and code generation make reusable pipelines cheaper to assemble. Reliable automation still depends on explicit definitions and tested routines.
tasks.still_hard: Missing data, changing account mappings, and causal interpretation require investigation. New questions can fall outside the reusable analysis templates.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a real business effect from an accounting change, selection bias, or unreliable measurement.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rebuilding extracts toward investigating unusual finance movements. A proposed added right is to initiate variance investigations within an agreed scope; financial approval rights do not change automatically.

reach.learn: Account mappings, posting cut-offs, reconciliation controls, and acceptable adjustment evidence.

evidence.claim: Versioned transformations, reconciliations, and statistical routines can execute deterministically; method choice remains contextual.
Genie supports questions over governed data using trusted assets; this supports prepared access, not unrestricted analytical correctness.
Uber documented faster query drafting while also reporting invented tables; generated queries need validation.

assumptions: The initial scope covers recurring finance analyses with stable source definitions.
Novel methods and unresolved data exceptions return to the data scientist.
Programming and analysis mostly occur in the {DATA_PLATFORM}; document-heavy priors do not imply document-based computation.
Build estimates cover a reusable starter for one finance dataset, not replacement of the data estate.
Access estimates include GDPR review where personal data is involved and employee consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which finance sources, connectors, and reconciliation totals are available.
How much work repeats an existing method versus develops a new one.
Whether personal or employee-level data is included.
Which investigation rights the financial manager would delegate.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the intended use.
research_questions: Which recurring analyses can use existing scheduling and connector configuration?
Do transformations reproduce historical totals across accounting periods?
Which missing-data patterns require investigation rather than an automatic default?
new_work: Review data quality exceptions and failed reconciliations.
Maintain source mappings and approved statistical templates.
Check changes to schemas, definitions, and access permissions.

tasks.short: Turn analysis results into clear, accurate finance visualizations.

steps.what: Clarify the audience, decision, measures, and comparison period.
Aggregate results and prepare chart measures and comparison groups.
Choose chart forms, scales, comparisons, and uncertainty displays.
Build charts, labels, filters, and page layouts.
Check figures, readability, accessibility, and potentially misleading visual choices.
Publish the approved view and set internal access.

tasks.design: Prepare reconciled chart datasets in the {DATA_PLATFORM} and configure reusable chart templates in the {BI}. Automated checks compare displayed measures with source results; reviewed views publish to an approved audience, while scheduled refreshes use the same tested definitions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts were rebuilt for each request, with inconsistent measure definitions and formatting. Existing visualization features still needed someone to prepare trustworthy inputs.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable semantic measures, chart templates, and automated rendering checks reduce assembly work. A language model is unnecessary for routine chart production.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing comparisons and communicating uncertainty remain contextual. Small groups, unusual distributions, and unfamiliar audiences need additional care.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when an accurate chart invites the wrong conclusion and redesign it around the actual decision.

ambition.what: Accessible budget variance views for department budget holders.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer formatting requests and more work testing whether people understand the charts. A proposed added right is to select visual standards for approved finance measures; publication and data-access authority remain subject to existing delegation.

reach.task: Maintain a certified finance reporting model.
reach.learn: Measure definitions, access rules, accessibility checks, and refresh dependencies.
Which comparisons lead to useful budget actions and which need accounting context.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports generated report pages on prepared semantic models; model preparation and review remain necessary.
Chart generation, scheduled refreshes, and numerical comparison checks can use configured software and deterministic code.
Clear visual comparisons, uncertainty displays, and accessibility require evaluation beyond checking numerical accuracy.

assumptions: The {BI} supports reusable templates, controlled access, and scheduled refreshes.
The initial scope uses approved finance measures and internal audiences.
Most assembly can be automated, while chart choice and final review retain human time.
Build estimates include access review and any applicable employee consultation under national rules.
GDPR applies where views contain personal data; employee-level monitoring requires separate assessment.
unknowns: Which measures already have agreed definitions.
Whether current {BI} permissions match the proposed audiences.
Whether charts expose small groups or individual staff performance.
Which accessibility requirements and visual standards are already adopted.
research_questions: Can configured chart templates cover the recurring visualization requests?
Do users correctly interpret uncertainty and comparison periods in sample views?
Can automated checks detect stale data, broken filters, and incorrect displayed totals?
new_work: Review new chart specifications and material changes.
Maintain templates, certified measures, and audience permissions.
Handle refresh failures and collect comprehension feedback.

tasks.short: Backtest finance models, investigate failures, and approve justified revisions.

steps.what: Define outcomes, validation periods, benchmarks, and acceptance criteria.
Freeze data versions and construct time-aware training and validation splits.
Run backtests, benchmarks, calibration checks, and relevant segment tests.
Investigate errors, leakage, instability, and business significance.
Revise features, assumptions, or model structure.
Repeat validation and compile the candidate comparison and limitations.
Review validation evidence and accept, reject, or request further work.
Register the approved version for the internal forecast process.

tasks.design: Build a versioned validation harness in the {DATA_PLATFORM} with frozen splits, benchmark comparisons, leakage checks, and reproducible report generation. The data scientist investigates failures and designs revisions; the {WORKFLOW} permits registration of a forecast model only after the financial manager records approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Validation code and evidence were rebuilt across models. Acceptance criteria and business costs were often implicit.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable testing components and faster code assembly reduce validation plumbing. Statistical validity and model reformulation still require expertise; training a predictive model does not require an autonomous language-model agent.
tasks.still_hard: Structural economic changes, rare outcomes, feedback effects, and unavailable future labels limit validation. A better historical score may fail to improve the finance decision.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when the target, assumptions, or business use is wrong despite apparently strong test results.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward investigating model failure and comparing justified alternatives. The scientist could gain authority to initiate recalibration reviews; approval to use a revised finance model remains with the designated approver.

reach.task: Challenge model assumptions and assess model limitations.
reach.learn: Independent validation, materiality, stress scenarios, and evidence needed for acceptance.

reach.task: Translate forecast errors into planning adjustments.
reach.learn: Planning horizons, asymmetric error costs, and actionable forecast tolerances.

evidence.claim: Backtests, fixed data splits, benchmark comparisons, and report tables can run deterministically after expert specification.
The PowerGPT trial separated model-assisted test selection from statistical-engine computation; its results do not establish autonomous finance model validation.
EU AI Act Annex III includes specified creditworthiness and life or health insurance pricing uses; intended use must be assessed.

assumptions: The baseline use is internal financial forecasting, hence the plan-to-forecast workflow.
The current process includes a financial manager approving business use; specialist independent validation may also be required.
Revisions return to investigation when validation fails; test sets are protected against repeated tuning.
Historical outcomes and reproducible model execution are available.
Build estimates include GDPR and EU AI Act use-case assessment, access, and applicable consultation under national rules.
Judgement-heavy reformulation keeps substantial human time despite the task's automation prior.
unknowns: Which model purposes, outcome labels, and forecast horizons apply.
Whether models affect creditworthiness, insurance pricing, employment, or other regulated decisions.
Who currently approves model use and whether independent validation is required.
Whether historical data can be reconstructed as it was known at each forecast date.
Which compute capacity and version controls are available.
research_questions: Do historical splits prevent temporal and entity leakage?
How stable are candidate rankings across periods, segments, and plausible stress conditions?
Which acceptance criteria reflect the cost of forecast error?
Can existing model registration and approval features cover the release controls?
new_work: Maintain benchmarks, validation datasets, and acceptance criteria.
Investigate failed tests, changing error patterns, and outcome-label delays.
Review release evidence and preserve rejected candidate histories.
Monitor approved models and schedule reassessment.

tasks.short: Explain analytical findings, answer finance questions, and record agreed decisions.

steps.what: Clarify the management decision, audience, and questions to address.
Assemble approved charts, figures, definitions, and limitations.
Draft the presentation narrative, implications, and speaker notes.

loop.input: Presentation brief and approved evidence pack with stable figure and chart references.
loop.output: Draft narrative and speaker notes with evidence references for substantive claims.
loop.check: Resolve every numerical reference against the evidence pack; flag unsupported claims for human review.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved claims remain flagged and the scientist completes them.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble figures but cannot adapt explanations and caveats to varied management questions.

steps.what: Verify claims, recommendations, uncertainty, and suitability for the audience.
Share the approved presentation with the intended internal audience.
Present findings, answer challenges, and discuss decision options.
Record agreed decisions, unresolved questions, owners, and due dates.

loop.input: Written discussion notes identifying explicitly agreed decisions and actions.
loop.output: Draft decision record and action list, with missing owners or dates marked.
loop.check: Each entry links to a note passage; the scientist confirms agreement, owners, and dates before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous entries return to manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes vary in wording; extraction helps without requiring recording or autonomous follow-up.

tasks.design: An evidence-linked generator assembles approved outputs from the {BI} and {DOCS}, then a bounded model loop drafts audience-specific explanations. The data scientist approves the pack before configured internal distribution through the {EMAIL}, leads the discussion, and reviews extracted decisions before they enter the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Presentation preparation mixed mechanical copying with audience-specific explanation. Generic templates could assemble slides but could not reliably express nuanced findings.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured evidence packs and bounded drafting make preparation easier to automate. They do not establish whether a recommendation is sound or secure stakeholder agreement.
tasks.still_hard: Live challenges, conflicting incentives, sensitive conclusions, and ambiguity about agreed actions require a person. Clear prose can still overstate weak evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, explain uncertainty under challenge, and help decision makers confront uncomfortable trade-offs.

ambition.what: Short finance decision clinics for department budget holders.

tasks.altitude: Preparation takes less of the week, leaving time for smaller decision discussions and follow-up questions. Presentation support does not confer authority to commit budgets or make management decisions.

reach.task: Frame a finance decision and compare feasible responses.
reach.learn: Decision thresholds, budget authority, timing constraints, and the evidence needed to act.

reach.task: Explain forecast changes to budget holders.
reach.learn: How to translate uncertainty into practical planning choices.

evidence.claim: Novo Nordisk documented drafting reports from approved text with human review; the vendor case supports assisted drafting, not equivalent finance savings.
Evidence-linked templates can assemble figures deterministically while a bounded model drafts explanatory text.
Live interpretation, stakeholder advice, and acceptance of recommendations require contextual human judgement.

assumptions: The baseline audience is internal management and finance users.
Approved numerical outputs exist before presentation drafting starts.
The model receives only data approved for its processing environment.
Decision extraction uses written notes; meeting recording is outside the initial scope.
Build estimates include access and confidentiality review, GDPR assessment where needed, and consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which presentation formats and evidence repositories are used.
Who may approve and distribute sensitive finance findings.
Whether an approved model-processing environment is available.
Whether management decisions require confirmation by a different role.
Whether budget holders want and can attend the proposed decision clinics.
research_questions: Can numerical claims be inserted as verified references rather than generated values?
How often do drafts omit caveats or turn associations into causal claims?
Can decision extraction distinguish proposals from explicitly agreed actions?
new_work: Review narratives, caveats, and evidence references.
Maintain presentation templates and drafting evaluation examples.
Resolve ambiguous decisions and missing action owners.
Check distribution permissions when audiences change.

role.altitude: The data scientist spends less time assembling datasets, charts, validation tables, and presentation packs. More time goes to investigating failure, selecting defensible methods, and advising finance users; budget and model-release authority change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Accountants and Auditors: investigate ledger anomalies using reconciled evidence.
Budget Analysts: connect forecast uncertainty to planning adjustments.
Financial Risk Specialists: challenge assumptions and define validation evidence.
Business Intelligence Analysts: maintain trusted finance measures and accessible views.
Financial Managers: frame decisions and discuss feasible responses.
skills_to_grow: Finance definitions, reconciliation controls, and accounting cut-offs.
Reproducible pipelines, data contracts, and deterministic validation.
Temporal validation, leakage detection, and uncertainty assessment.
Bounded model evaluation, privacy, and use-case-specific AI governance.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring finance decision service that combines reconciled analysis, monitored forecasts, accessible variance views, and short decision clinics. Start with one finance process and expand after its evidence, access, and approval controls work reliably.
